Definition: comparative of a derivative of G430; more endurable:--more tolerable.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus says it shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for the city that rejects His disciples. The word is a comparison of judgment: some refusals are worse than others, and the judgment fits the light that was refused.
TheologicalSignificance: One comparison about tolerable judgment carries no system of its own; its warning is Jesus', that rejecting the gospel after hearing it is worse than never having heard.
